_doc: Bodies for the target picker, globe ellipsoids and basemaps. See CONTRACTS.md section 3. Radii: IAU WGCCRE 2015 (a, b, c in metres) for planets, satellites, Ceres and Vesta; published shape-model/flyby values for small bodies (see _sources). mean_radius_m is the IAU mean radius where defined, otherwise the volume-equivalent radius. Every basemap was fetched on its verified date.
_sources: Archinal et al. 2018, Report of the IAU Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements: 2015, Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy 130:22, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10569-017-9805-5
NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE body ID codes, https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/toolkit_docs/C/req/naif_ids.html
NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics, Planetary Satellite Physical Parameters and small-body database, https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/
Thomas 2010 Icarus 208 and Thomas et al. 2013 Icarus 226 (Saturn small moons); Weaver et al. 2016 Science 351 (Pluto small moons)

Watanabe et al. 2019 Science 364 (Ryugu); Barnouin et al. 2019 Nature Geoscience 12 (Bennu); Daly et al. 2023 Nature 616 and Naidu et al. 2020 Icarus 348 (Didymos/Dimorphos); Stern et al. 2019 Science 364 (Arrokoth); Ostro et al. 1999 Icarus 137 (Toutatis); Shepard et al. 2021 PSJ 2 (Psyche)

NASA GIBS, https://nasa-gibs.github.io/gibs-api-docs/; Esri World Imagery; OpenStreetMap tile usage policy https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/; EOX s2maps.eu; OpenPlanetaryMap https://www.openplanetary.org/opm
Thumbnails: Wikimedia Commons copies of NASA/JPL/USGS/ESA images, credits in web/img/bodies/CREDITS.md

bodies.name: Sun
bodies.summary: The Sun is the G2V star at the centre of the Solar System, observed from space by SDO, SOHO, STEREO, Hinode, Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.summary: Mercury is the innermost planet, mapped globally by the MESSENGER orbiter (2011-2015) and now studied by ESA/JAXA BepiColombo.

bodies.name: Phobos
bodies.summary: Phobos is the larger and inner moon of Mars, mapped by Viking, Mars Express HRSC/SRC and MRO HiRISE.

bodies.summary: Deimos is the smaller and outer moon of Mars, imaged by Viking, Mars Express and MRO HiRISE.

bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.summary: Ceres is the largest main-belt object and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System, mapped globally by the Dawn framing camera in 2015-2018.

basemaps.name: Dawn FC global mosaic
basemaps.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA (Dawn FC); via NASA Solar System Treks

basemaps.name: Dawn FC HAMO color hillshade
basemaps.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA (Dawn FC); via NASA Solar System Treks

bodies.name: Vesta
bodies.summary: Vesta is the second most massive main-belt asteroid, a differentiated protoplanet mapped by Dawn in 2011-2012.

basemaps.name: Dawn FC HAMO mosaic
basemaps.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA (Dawn FC); via NASA Solar System Treks

basemaps.name: Dawn color hillshade
basemaps.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA (Dawn FC); via NASA Solar System Treks

bodies.name: Psyche
bodies.summary: Psyche is a large metal-rich M-type main-belt asteroid targeted by NASA's Psyche orbiter, launched in October 2023, with arrival expected in 2029.

bodies.name: Lutetia
bodies.summary: Lutetia is a large main-belt asteroid flown past by ESA's Rosetta in July 2010 at 3,160 km.

bodies.name: Šteins
bodies.summary: Šteins is a small E-type main-belt asteroid imaged by Rosetta during its September 2008 flyby.

bodies.name: Gaspra
bodies.summary: Gaspra is a small S-type main-belt asteroid, the first asteroid imaged close-up by a spacecraft (Galileo, October 1991).

bodies.name: Ida (and Dactyl)
bodies.summary: Ida is an S-type main-belt asteroid with the small moon Dactyl, flown past by Galileo in August 1993.

bodies.name: Mathilde
bodies.summary: Mathilde is a dark C-type main-belt asteroid flown past by NEAR Shoemaker in June 1997.

bodies.name: Annefrank
bodies.summary: Annefrank is a small main-belt asteroid imaged by Stardust during its November 2002 flyby.

bodies.name: Braille
bodies.summary: Braille is a small Mars-crossing asteroid flown past by Deep Space 1 in July 1999.

bodies.name: Dinkinesh (and Selam)
bodies.summary: Dinkinesh is a small main-belt asteroid with a contact-binary satellite (Selam) discovered by NASA's Lucy during its November 2023 flyby.

bodies.name: Donaldjohanson
bodies.summary: Donaldjohanson is an elongated main-belt asteroid flown past by NASA's Lucy in April 2025.

bodies.name: Other asteroids
bodies.summary: Group entry for all other asteroids (e.g. Pallas, Hygiea, Kleopatra, Jupiter Trojans) and for catch-all asteroid datasets and small-body archives.

bodies.name: Eros
bodies.summary: Eros is a large S-type near-Earth asteroid orbited and landed on by NEAR Shoemaker in 2000-2001.

bodies.name: Itokawa
bodies.summary: Itokawa is a small peanut-shaped near-Earth asteroid visited by JAXA's Hayabusa in 2005, the first asteroid sample-return target.

bodies.name: Ryugu
bodies.summary: Ryugu is a carbonaceous top-shaped near-Earth asteroid visited by JAXA's Hayabusa2 in 2018-2019, which returned samples to Earth in December 2020.

basemaps.name: Hayabusa2 ONC-T v-band global mosaic
basemaps.attribution: JAXA, University of Tokyo and collaborators (Hayabusa2 ONC-T); via NASA Solar System Treks

bodies.name: Bennu
bodies.summary: Bennu is a rubble-pile carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid mapped by NASA's OSIRIS-REx in 2018-2021, which returned samples in September 2023.

bodies.name: Didymos
bodies.summary: Didymos is a near-Earth binary asteroid whose small moon Dimorphos was targeted by NASA's DART impactor in September 2022.

bodies.name: Dimorphos
bodies.summary: Dimorphos is the small moon of the binary asteroid Didymos, impacted by DART on 26 September 2022 and due to be revisited by ESA's Hera spacecraft (arrival December 2026).

bodies.name: Toutatis
bodies.summary: Toutatis is an elongated tumbling near-Earth asteroid imaged by radar and flown past by Chang'e 2 in December 2012.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.summary: Jupiter is the largest planet, imaged by Voyager, Galileo, Cassini, New Horizons, Juno and Hubble/JWST.

basemaps.name: Cassini ISS map (USGS)

bodies.name: Io
bodies.summary: Io is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System, imaged by Voyager, Galileo, New Horizons and Juno.

bodies.name: Europa
bodies.summary: Europa is an ice-covered Jovian moon with a subsurface ocean, imaged by Galileo, Voyager and Juno and the target of Europa Clipper and JUICE.

bodies.name: Ganymede
bodies.summary: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System and has its own magnetic field, imaged by Voyager, Galileo and Juno and targeted by ESA's JUICE.

basemaps.name: Voyager/Galileo mosaic

bodies.name: Callisto
bodies.summary: Callisto is a heavily cratered Jovian moon imaged by Voyager and Galileo and visited by JUICE flybys.

basemaps.name: Galileo/Voyager mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Amalthea
bodies.summary: Amalthea is a small, irregular inner moon of Jupiter imaged by Voyager 1 and Galileo.

bodies.name: Himalia
bodies.summary: Himalia is the largest irregular moon of Jupiter, imaged at long range by Cassini, New Horizons and Juno.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.summary: Saturn is the ringed gas giant, orbited by Cassini from 2004 to 2017 and observed by Voyager, Hubble and JWST.

basemaps.name: Cassini ISS map (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Mimas
bodies.summary: Mimas is a small inner moon of Saturn dominated by Herschel crater, imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

basemaps.name: Cassini ISS mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Enceladus
bodies.summary: Enceladus is a small icy moon of Saturn with active south-polar water plumes, extensively imaged by Cassini.

bodies.name: Tethys
bodies.summary: Tethys is a mid-sized icy moon of Saturn with a giant impact crater (Odysseus) and a long canyon (Ithaca Chasma), imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

basemaps.name: Cassini ISS mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Dione
bodies.summary: Dione is a mid-sized icy moon of Saturn imaged by Voyager and Cassini, with bright wispy terrain on its trailing hemisphere.

basemaps.name: Cassini/Voyager mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Rhea
bodies.summary: Rhea is Saturn's second-largest moon, a heavily cratered icy world imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

basemaps.name: Cassini/Voyager mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Titan
bodies.summary: Titan is Saturn's largest moon with a dense nitrogen atmosphere and hydrocarbon lakes, mapped by Cassini ISS, VIMS and RADAR and sampled by the Huygens probe.

bodies.name: Hyperion
bodies.summary: Hyperion is an irregular, chaotically tumbling, sponge-like moon of Saturn imaged by Voyager 2 and Cassini.

basemaps.name: Voyager 2 mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Iapetus
bodies.summary: Iapetus is a Saturnian moon with a dark leading hemisphere, a bright trailing hemisphere and an equatorial ridge, imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

basemaps.name: Cassini/Voyager mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Phoebe
bodies.summary: Phoebe is a retrograde irregular moon of Saturn, flown past by Cassini in June 2004.

basemaps.name: Cassini ISS mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Janus
bodies.summary: Janus is a small co-orbital inner moon of Saturn that swaps orbits with Epimetheus, imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

bodies.name: Epimetheus
bodies.summary: Epimetheus is a small co-orbital inner moon of Saturn that swaps orbits with Janus, imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

bodies.name: Prometheus
bodies.summary: Prometheus is an elongated shepherd moon on the inner edge of Saturn's F ring, imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

bodies.name: Pandora
bodies.summary: Pandora is a small shepherd moon on the outer edge of Saturn's F ring, imaged by Voyager and Cassini.

bodies.name: Pan
bodies.summary: Pan is a tiny ravioli-shaped moon in Saturn's Encke Gap, imaged by Cassini.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.summary: Uranus is the tilted ice giant, visited only by Voyager 2 in January 1986 and observed by Hubble, Keck and JWST.

basemaps.name: Voyager/HST map (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Miranda
bodies.summary: Miranda is a small Uranian moon with extreme patchwork terrain and the giant cliff Verona Rupes, imaged by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Ariel
bodies.summary: Ariel is a Uranian moon with extensive canyons and valleys, imaged by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Umbriel
bodies.summary: Umbriel is a dark, ancient, heavily cratered moon of Uranus imaged by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Titania
bodies.summary: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, imaged by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Oberon
bodies.summary: Oberon is the outermost large moon of Uranus, imaged by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.summary: Neptune is the outermost planet, visited only by Voyager 2 in August 1989 and observed by Hubble, Keck and JWST.

basemaps.name: Voyager/HST map (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Triton
bodies.summary: Triton is Neptune's large retrograde moon, a probable captured Kuiper Belt object with active nitrogen geysers, imaged by Voyager 2.

basemaps.name: Voyager 2 mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Proteus
bodies.summary: Proteus is Neptune's largest inner moon, an irregular dark body imaged by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Nereid
bodies.summary: Nereid is an outer irregular moon of Neptune with a highly eccentric orbit, resolved only as a few pixels by Voyager 2.

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.summary: Pluto is a Kuiper Belt dwarf planet imaged globally in 2015 by NASA's New Horizons.

basemaps.name: New Horizons LORRI/MVIC mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Charon
bodies.summary: Charon is Pluto's largest moon, about half its size, imaged by New Horizons in 2015.

basemaps.name: New Horizons LORRI/MVIC mosaic (USGS)
basemaps.attribution: USGS Astrogeology Science Center, NASA and mission teams (planetarymaps.usgs.gov)

bodies.name: Nix
bodies.summary: Nix is a small irregular moon of Pluto imaged by New Horizons.

bodies.name: Hydra
bodies.summary: Hydra is a small irregular outer moon of Pluto imaged by New Horizons.

bodies.name: Arrokoth
bodies.summary: Arrokoth is a bilobed contact-binary Kuiper Belt object flown past by New Horizons on 1 January 2019.

bodies.name: Other Kuiper Belt objects
bodies.summary: Group entry for other Kuiper Belt and trans-Neptunian objects (e.g. Eris, Haumea, Makemake, Quaoar, Sedna, Centaurs) and for catch-all TNO datasets.

bodies.name: 1P/Halley
bodies.summary: 1P/Halley is the best-known periodic comet, imaged at close range by the Giotto, Vega 1 and Vega 2 probes in March 1986.

bodies.name: 19P/Borrelly
bodies.summary: 19P/Borrelly is a Jupiter-family comet flown past by Deep Space 1 in September 2001.

bodies.name: 81P/Wild 2
bodies.summary: 81P/Wild 2 is a Jupiter-family comet flown past by Stardust in January 2004, which returned coma dust samples to Earth in 2006.

bodies.name: 9P/Tempel 1
bodies.summary: 9P/Tempel 1 is a Jupiter-family comet impacted by Deep Impact in July 2005 and revisited by Stardust-NExT in February 2011.

bodies.name: 103P/Hartley 2
bodies.summary: 103P/Hartley 2 is a small hyperactive Jupiter-family comet flown past by EPOXI in November 2010.

bodies.name: 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko
bodies.summary: 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko is the Jupiter-family comet orbited by ESA's Rosetta (2014-2016), which landed Philae on its surface.

bodies.name: 3I/ATLAS
bodies.summary: 3I/ATLAS is the third confirmed interstellar object, discovered in July 2025 and observed during its 2025-2026 passage by Hubble, JWST, Mars orbiters and ground telescopes.

bodies.name: Other comets
bodies.summary: Group entry for all other comets and interstellar objects (e.g. Hale-Bopp, Shoemaker-Levy 9, 2I/Borisov, 1I/ʻOumuamua) and for catch-all comet datasets.

bodies.name: Planetary rings
bodies.summary: Group entry for planetary ring systems (Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune and small-body rings) used by ring-specific datasets such as Cassini ISS, VIMS and UVIS ring observations and occultations.
